title: O Living Bread from Heaven
description: O Living Bread from Heaven in Tonic Solfa to EWING, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Johann Rist wrote these words in German. Catherine Winkworth's translation was printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (St. Louis, 1927), as hymn 435.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens and Sixes Double (7.6.7.6.7.6.7.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to EWING; any other Sevens and Sixes Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: O liv-ing Bread from hea-ven, How hast Thou fed Thy guest! The gifts Thou now hast giv-en Have filled my heart with rest. O won-drous Food of bless-ing! O Cup that heals our woes! My heart, this gift pos-sess-ing, In thank-ful song o’er-flows.

lines: How hast Thou fed Thy guest!
The gifts Thou now hast given
Have filled my heart with rest.
O Cup that heals our woes!
My Lord, Thou here hast led me
And there Thyself hast fed me
The Bread of life from heaven,
That now I shall not die.
Ah, Lord, I do not merit
And all my soul and spirit
Lord, grant me that, thus strengthened
My course on earth is lengthened,
And when Thou call’st my spirit

licence: Public domain: Johann Rist died in 1667; Catherine Winkworth died in 1878.
credits: Words by Johann Rist (1607–1667), translated by Catherine Winkworth (1827–1878), public domain, as printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (1927); set to EWING by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
